analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is at head lines 2057-2058. It is a documentation sentence that adds test coverage of a `required` CI lane, which keeps its fallback without asking while job sizes are off. It alters no code, workflow, protocol, key handling, authorization or cache behavior. I read both units, which are mostly unchanged developer test documentation. They touch the provider cache, attestation and cluster test areas only as prose. The prose does not change any control described in the threat model (T-041 prefix-cache storage, TB-011 App Attest authorization, TB-002 coordinator-to-provider WebSocket). The routing-test text covers CI runner routing (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py), which is outside the provider threat boundaries and has no assets here. The doc says the test uses a loopback HTTPS plane and contacts no real plane, which is consistent with a non-production test. Whether the described `required` lane behavior is implemented correctly in the CI route script and its test is not visible in this PR excerpt. This is a docs-only change, so it is not a security concern and creates no threat-model gap.
